A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LD-SMC with the same title and authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and FFHQ reconstruction experiments, quantitative results in Tables 1–2 and Appendix D, and a guidance-threshold study.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, expanded benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and runtime and memory measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v2 changes the Gibbs procedure to update full latent trajectories, initializes SMC particles from the standard-normal prior instead of around the forward trajectory's endpoint, and samples the final chain by weights instead of selecting the highest-weight particle (Section 4.2; Algorithm 1). Below threshold s, it combines both guidance terms using rho, whereas v1 switched exclusively to auxiliary guidance. Initial and final weighting rules also change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and FFHQ on box inpainting, Gaussian deblurring and 8× super-resolution. v2 adds free-form inpainting on both datasets, introducing irregular missing-pixel patterns within the existing image-restoration coverage (Tables 1–2; Appendix H).

E2.justification: v2 adds PFLD and LatentDAPS to the benchmark comparisons, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives. PFLD was discussed but explicitly not compared in v1. Latent DPS/TDS become LDPS/LTDS, and Resample becomes ReSample; these renamed comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 revises hyperparameter-search grids and evaluates LD-SMC with both one and five particles, adding particle-count, Gibbs-iteration and computational-cost protocols. Appendix A specifies settings for the new baselines. Section 5.1 also states CIN256-V2 for ImageNet instead of v1's VQ-4; this is a reported setting revision, although the PDFs do not establish whether it corrects documentation or reflects a model change in executed experiments.

E4.justification: v1's principal ablation varies the guidance-switch threshold (Table 3). v2 revises that sweep and adds particle-count sensitivity, multiple Gibbs iterations on super-resolution and deblurring, and prior-versus-DPS-versus-LD-SMC proposal comparisons (Figures 5–6; Appendix F, Table 5). Appendix E additionally measures computational scaling with particles and Gibbs iterations.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that runtime and memory measurements are averaged over 10 trials (Appendix E). v1 provides no corresponding repeated-trial reporting. Neither version reports image-quality confidence intervals, error bars or seed-based uncertainty; the new trial count concerns computational measurements.

E6.justification: Numerous retained benchmark entries change alongside substantial new results. For five-particle LD-SMC, ImageNet box-inpainting FID/NIQE changes from 51.81/5.103 to 50.67/6.891, and FFHQ deblurring FID changes from 32.18 to 29.47. v2 also adds free-form, new-baseline, one-particle, ablation and computational results. Because the procedure and reported settings change, these are revised results rather than isolated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 contains posterior approximations and a recursive derivation but no convergence proof. v2 revises the generative and target distributions, derives endpoint cases, and adds Theorem 4.1 and Appendix C's Gibbs-stationarity and SMC-convergence arguments with explicit assumptions. Separately, Eq. 7 replaces squared-error gradients with log-likelihood gradients while retaining subtraction, which is not equivalent with Appendix D's positive coefficients.

C1.justification: v2 adds asymptotically accurate posterior sampling as an explicit central contribution in the introduction and Theorem 4.1. v1 claims an approximate sampling method and empirical advantages without this guarantee. The emphasis on improved inpainting remains, with v2's contribution statement more specifically emphasizing perceptual quality.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for inconsistent improvements at small particle counts, relates Gibbs-iteration tradeoffs to threshold s, and discusses unoptimized code and computational scaling. Appendix C acknowledges that its gradient assumptions may fail even for linear transformations. These extend the existing interpretations of perceptual-versus-distortion tradeoffs and auxiliary guidance without replacing their central meaning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a stated public code link, selected hyperparameters for each dataset/task in Table 3, the 64-image tuning-sample size, initialization details, and comparator-specific settings in Appendix A. Table 4 supplies concrete runtime and memory information where v1 offered only qualitative computational limitations. These substantially expand reproducibility information; actual code availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against ADIR, variational approaches, DAPS, MGPS and SILO, alongside additional SMC references. It reframes SMC-Diff's limitation around expensive prior proposals and explicitly distinguishes LD-SMC's claimed asymptotic guarantees from PFLD (Section 3). This goes beyond citation or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introductory motivation and sampling exposition, organizing the latter around target distributions, weights, proposals and Algorithm 1. Derivations move into dedicated appendices, the appendix structure is expanded and reorganized, and the separate Limitations section is incorporated into the conclusion. These changes exceed local language polishing.

P2.justification: v2 expands benchmark tables with another task and additional method rows, adds hyperparameter, cost and proposal-ablation tables, and replaces the threshold table with a plot alongside new sensitivity plots. Reconstruction grids are revised to include free-form masks and additional baselines. Existing graphical-model and appendix illustrations are also relocated or revised; they are not all new content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the method's component choices and practical tradeoffs: v1's single threshold study and qualitative cost warning are supplemented by particle, Gibbs and proposal ablations, measured costs, broader comparisons and selected implementation settings. These gains make the empirical contribution considerably easier to assess and reproduce. The improvement is qualified by Eq. 7's guidance-sign inconsistency and by the convergence proof's larger-proposal-variance assumption, which does not cover the stated equal-variance default.
